p.i: An account of Lehi’s death. Nephi’s brothers rebel against him. The Lord warns Nephi to go away into the wilderness. His travels in the wilderness, and so forth.

chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 After I Nephi finished teaching my brothers, our father Lehi also said many things to them, recounting to them how the Lord had done great things for them through leaving the land of Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse2 He talked to them about their rebellion during the sea voyage and God’s mercy in sparing their lives, so that they weren’t lying at the bottom of the sea. VerseEnd Verse3 He also spoke to them about the promised land they had been given: how merciful the Lord had been in warning us to flee from the land of Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse4 He said: I’ve seen a vision showing me Jerusalem has been destroyed. If we had remained there, we also would have died. VerseEnd Verse5 But, he said, despite our hardships, we’ve been given a promised land, a land specially chosen over all other lands, a land the Lord God has covenanted with me that my descendants will inherit. Indeed, the Lord has consecrated this land for my children and me forever, and also for those who will likewise be led out of other countries by the Lord’s power. VerseEnd Verse6 Therefore I prophesy under the influence of God’s Spirit over me, that no one will come to this land unless they’re brought by the Lord’s power. VerseEnd Verse7 So this land is consecrated to those He’ll bring here. And if they serve Him according to the commandments He has given, it will always be a land of liberty for them; therefore they’ll never be brought down into captivity — but if they are, it will be because of iniquity; because if iniquity abounds, the land will become cursed because of their failure to serve Him. It will always be blessed for the righteous. VerseEnd Verse8 It’s a wise thing for this land to still be kept from other nations knowing about it. Otherwise, many nations would overrun this land, so there wouldn’t be any place for an inheritance. VerseEnd

Verse9 As a result, I’ve obtained a promise that to the degree they keep His commandments — including anyone the Lord God brings from the land of Jerusalem — they’ll prosper in this land. And they’ll be hidden from all other nations, so they can have this land to themselves. And if they keep His commandments, they’ll be blessed upon this land. No one will interfere or take away the land they receive as an inheritance; they’ll live here safely forever. VerseEnd Verse10 But when they fall away in unbelief, after having received such great blessings from the Lord, having knowledge about the earth’s creation and mankind’s history, knowing the great and awe-inspiring things the Lord has done since the world was created, having power given to them to live by faith, having all the commandments from the beginning, and having been brought by His infinite goodness into this precious land of promise — I say if the time comes that they choose to reject the Holy One of Israel, the true Messiah, their Redeemer and their God, the judgments of Him who is righteous will fall upon them. VerseEnd Verse11 He’ll bring other nations to them, He’ll give to these others power and He’ll take their lands away from them. He will scatter and strike them down. VerseEnd Verse12 Indeed, as one generation passes to another, there will be slaughter and God’s punishment as a reminder for them.

Therefore, my sons, I want 2PP you to remember; I want 2PP you to listen to me carefully. VerseEnd Verse13 I wish 2PP you would wake up, wake up from 2PP your deep sleep — the sleep of hell — and shake off the awful chains that restrain 2PP you, the spiritual chains that overtake people to enslave them, leading down to the endless abyss of misery and anguish. VerseEnd Verse14 Wake up, get up from the dust, and hear a trembling parent’s words, whose body 2PP you’ll soon bury in the cold, silent grave, from where no traveler returns. A few days from now I will die, leaving my life here like everything does on this earth. VerseEnd Verse15 But the Lord has redeemed my soul from hell. I’ve seen His glory, and I’m continually welcomed in the arms of His love. VerseEnd Verse16 I want 2PP you to remember to keep the Lord’s statutes and judgments. This has been a deep concern of mine from the beginning. VerseEnd Verse17 My heart has been weighed down with sorrow from time to time, as I’ve been afraid that — because of the hardness of 2PP your hearts — the Lord who is God will have no choice but to punish 2PP you in His justified wrath, and cut 2PP you off and destroy 2PP you forever. VerseEnd Verse18 Then a cursing would follow 2PP your descendants for many generations, killing them by sword and famines because of anger and hatred that enslaves through iniquity because they rebel against God and follow the accuser. VerseEnd Verse19 My sons, may these things not come upon 2PP you! Instead, may 2PP you be a chosen and blessed people of the Lord.

May 2PP you do His will, because His ways are righteousness forever. VerseEnd Verse20 He has said: To the degree 2PP you keep My commandments, 2PP you’ll prosper in the land. But to the degree 2PP you don’t keep My commandments, 2PP you’ll be shut out from My presence. VerseEnd Verse21 And now, so that I can have joy in 2PP you, so my heart can gladly leave this world thinking of 2PP you, and so I don’t die filled with grief and sorrow — get up from the dust, my sons, and be men, determined in one mind and one heart, united in all things, so 2PP you don’t fall into captivity VerseEnd Verse22 and aren’t afflicted with a severe cursing and don’t provoke a righteous God’s judgment upon 2PP you to the eternal destruction of both spirit and body. VerseEnd Verse23 Wake up, my sons, clothe yourselves with righteousness, shake off the chains that bind 2PP you, come out of the darkness, and get up from the dust. VerseEnd Verse24 Don’t rebel anymore against 2PP your brother, whose understanding and teaching have been glorious, who’s kept God’s commandments since we left Jerusalem, and who’s been an instrument in God’s hands in bringing us to the promised land. Had it not been for him, we would certainly have died of hunger in the wilderness. Nevertheless, 2PP you tried to kill him, and 2PP you’ve constantly hurt and fought him. VerseEnd Verse25 I’m very afraid and worried about 2PP you, expecting 2PP you’ll make him suffer again. 2PP You’ve accused him of trying to get power and authority over 2PP you. But I know he hasn’t tried to get power and authority over 2PP you; on the contrary, he has sought God’s glory and 2PP your own eternal happiness. VerseEnd Verse26 But 2PP you’ve complained because he’s been forthright with 2PP you. 2PP You say he has reprimanded 2PP you harshly and been angry with 2PP you. But his powerful rebuke came from God’s word within him. And what 2PP you call anger was the truth of God, which he didn’t hold back, honestly declaring 2PP your iniquities. VerseEnd Verse27 God’s power was clearly with him, to such an extent that when he commanded 2PP you then 2PP you obeyed. That wasn’t just him, but it was the Spirit of the Lord in him that led him to speak, so he couldn’t remain silent. VerseEnd

Verse28 Now, my sons Laman, Lemuel, and Sam, as well as my sons who are Ishmael’s sons, if 2PP you’ll listen to Nephi teach, 2PP you won’t be lost. If 2PP you’re willing to listen to him, I leave 2PP you a blessing, namely my first blessing. VerseEnd Verse29 But if 2PP you refuse to listen to him, I’ll take away my first blessing — even my entire blessing — and it will rest upon him. VerseEnd Verse30 Now Zoram, I speak to 2PSF you: 2PSI You are Laban’s servant; nevertheless, 2PSI you’ve been brought out of the land of Jerusalem. I know 2PSI you are a true friend to my son Nephi forever. VerseEnd Verse31 Because 2PSI you’ve been faithful, 2PSI your descendants will be blessed with his descendants — they’ll live long upon this land in prosperity. And nothing but their own iniquity will harm or disturb their prosperity on this land forever. VerseEnd Verse32 Therefore if 2PP you keep the Lord’s commandments, the Lord has consecrated this land for the security of 2PSI your descendants with my son’s descendants. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 Now Jacob, I speak to 2PSF you: 2PSI You are my first born during the times of my trouble and difficulties in the wilderness. In 2PSI your childhood 2PSI you’ve experienced hardships and a great deal of distress because of 2PSI your brothers’ harsh and violent behavior. VerseEnd Verse2 Nevertheless, my first born in the wilderness, 2PSI you are familiar with the greatness of God. He’ll consecrate 2PSI your difficulties ultimately to benefit 2PSI you. VerseEnd Verse3 Therefore 2PSI your soul will be blessed, and 2PSI you’ll live safely with 2PSI your brother Nephi, and 2PSI your life will be spent serving God. Therefore I know 2PSI you are redeemed because of the righteousness of 2PSI your Redeemer, for 2PSI you’ve seen that He’ll come at the appointed time to bring salvation to mankind. VerseEnd Verse4 2PSI You’ve seen His glory in 2PSI your youth, so 2PSI you are blessed just like those He’ll minister to personally on earth. Because the Spirit is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and the way is prepared since the Fall of mankind, and salvation is free. VerseEnd Verse5 People are instructed well enough to understand good from evil — the law is given to mankind. However, no one on earth is justified by the law — that is, mankind are cut off by the law, indeed, they were cut off by the earthly, temporal law. Likewise, they’re shut out from good things by the spiritual law and become miserable forever. VerseEnd Verse6 This is because redemption comes in and through the Holy Messiah, because He is full of grace and truth. VerseEnd Verse7 He offers Himself as a sacrifice for sin, to fulfill the requirements of the law for all those who have a broken heart and a contrite spirit. Therefore the requirements of the law cannot be met for anyone else. VerseEnd Verse8 That being the case, how extremely important it is to declare these things to the inhabitants of the earth, so they can know that no flesh can live in God’s presence except through the merits, mercy, and grace of the Holy Messiah, who lays down His mortal life, and takes it back by the power of the Spirit, so He can accomplish the resurrection of the dead, being the first who will rise from the grave. VerseEnd Verse9 He is the essential required sacrificial offering to God, since He’ll intercede on behalf of all mankind; and those who believe in Him will be saved. VerseEnd Verse10 Because of the intercession for everyone, all mankind will be brought to God. They’ll stand in His presence to be judged by Him according to the truth and holiness in Him.

The Holy One has established the requirements of the law that impose a fixed punishment opposite to the available happiness. Happiness is the purpose of the atonement. VerseEnd Verse11 But there must be a balance or opposition for all things. If there were no balance, my first born in the wilderness, righteousness and wickedness couldn’t exist, or happiness and misery, or good and bad. The result would be no contrast but only an unvarying sameness. That being the case, if everything were fixed into the same condition, there would be no difference between life or death, decay or growth, happiness or misery, awareness or unconsciousness. VerseEnd Verse12 Therefore everything would have been created for nothing — there would have been no purpose resulting from its creation. This failure to have opposites would destroy the wisdom of God and His eternal purposes, and also make the power, mercy, and justice of God mean nothing. VerseEnd Verse13 If 2PG you eliminate law, 2PG you must also eliminate sin. And if 2PG you eliminate sin, 2PG you must also eliminate righteousness. Then if there’s no righteousness, there’s no happiness. And if there’s no righteousness or happiness, there’s no punishment or misery. And if all these plans of God are destroyed, 2PG you must also destroy God. If 2PG you destroy God, then we wouldn’t exist, and neither would the earth, since there couldn’t have been a creation of things, either to act or be acted upon; therefore all things would have necessarily ceased to exist. VerseEnd

Verse14 Now, my sons, I tell 2PP you these things to help and instruct 2PP you. Because there is a God and He has created all things: the heavens, the earth, and everything that’s in them, both things to act and things to be acted upon. VerseEnd Verse15 And to bring about His eternal plans in His purpose for mankind — after He had created our first parents and the animals of the field and the birds of the air and, in short, all created things — there had to be a contrast: the forbidden fruit in opposition to the tree of life, the one sweet and the other bitter. VerseEnd Verse16 Therefore the Lord God gave mankind the ability to choose; but people couldn’t choose unless they were presented with a decision to make. VerseEnd

Verse17 And based on what I’ve read, I must conclude an angel of God, according to what’s written, fell from heaven. And he became the accuser, having pursued what was evil before God. VerseEnd Verse18 And because he fell from heaven and became miserable forever, he wants mankind to be miserable too. Indeed, that old serpent — who is the accuser, who is the father of all lies — said to Eve: Eat some of the forbidden fruit, and 2PP you won’t die, but 2PP you’ll be like God, knowing good and evil. VerseEnd Verse19 After Adam and Eve ate the forbidden fruit, they were driven out of the Garden of Eden to cultivate the earth. VerseEnd Verse20 Then, they had children, which is the family of the whole earth. VerseEnd Verse21 And mankind’s lifespan was lengthened, according to God’s will, so they could repent while living on earth. Therefore their condition became a probation, and their lives were lengthened to provide them time to keep the commandments the Lord God gave mankind. He commanded that everyone must repent, letting everyone know they were lost because of their parents’ transgression. VerseEnd

Verse22 Now if Adam hadn’t transgressed, he wouldn’t have fallen, but he would have stayed in the Garden of Eden. And all things that were created must have remained in exactly the same state as when first created. They would have continued forever and had no end, VerseEnd Verse23 and they wouldn’t have had children. Therefore they would have remained in a state of innocence, having no joy, because they knew no misery, doing no good, because they weren’t exposed to sin. VerseEnd Verse24 But all things have been done in the wisdom of Him who knows all things. VerseEnd Verse25 Adam fell for people to exist, and we exist to experience joy. VerseEnd Verse26 And the Messiah comes at the appointed time to rescue mankind from the Fall. Then because they’re rescued from the Fall, they’re free to act, knowing good from evil, to act for themselves and not to be acted on. However, mankind will be punished based on the law on the great and last day, according to the commandments God has given. VerseEnd Verse27 So people act freely in this life, and this creation lets people choose freely. They’re free to choose liberty and eternal life by obeying mankind’s Mediator, or instead choose captivity and death by letting the accuser lead them. The accuser wants all mankind to become miserable like he is. VerseEnd

Verse28 Now, my sons, I want 2PP you to look to the great Mediator and follow His great commandments and be faithful to His words and choose eternal life according to the will of His Holy Spirit, VerseEnd Verse29 and not choose eternal death according to the will of our fallen and vulnerable bodies, with their weaknesses and appetites, which allows the accuser to tempt and mislead 2PP you to fall into hell, so he can rule over 2PP you in his own kingdom. VerseEnd Verse30 I’ve spoken these few words to all of 2PP you, my sons, in the final days of my life. I’ve chosen to follow those good principles taught in the prophets’ words. I have no other objective than 2PP your souls’ everlasting happiness. Amen. VerseEnd
